lean.statement:
∀ {E : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace E]
  [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [inst_4 : MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E] (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure E)
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] (C : ℝ),
  (∀ (v : E → ℝ),
      ContDiff ℝ (↑⊤) v →
        HasCompactSupport v →
          ∫ (x : E), v x ^ 2 * Real.log (v x ^ 2) ∂μ - (∫ (x : E), v x ^ 2 ∂μ) * Real.log (∫ (x : E), v x ^ 2 ∂μ) ≤
            2 * C * ∫ (x : E), ‖gradient v x‖ ^ 2 ∂μ) →
    ∀ (f : E → ℝ),
      ContDiff ℝ (↑⊤) f →
        HasCompactSupport f →
          AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.FunctionalInequalities.Poincare.Admissible μ f ∧
            AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.FunctionalInequalities.Poincare.variance μ f ≤
              C * AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.FunctionalInequalities.Poincare.dirichletEnergy μ f
approved_definition_context: The embedded infinite natural differentiability index denotes all finite derivative orders, not analyticity.

Poincare.Admissible μ f means that f, its squared centered value, and its squared genuine gradient norm are all integrable. Poincare.variance is the integral of the squared centered value; Poincare.dirichletEnergy is the integral of the squared gradient norm.
